title: Generative AI in Higher Education: The ChatGPT Effect
extended_summary:
This book-length work addresses the rapid emergence of ChatGPT and generative AI in higher education and asks how these tools might reshape teaching, learning, assessment, and institutional policy. Rather than evaluating a single intervention on learning outcomes, it synthesizes concepts, examples, and practices to help educators and policymakers understand the opportunities and risks of GenAI in academic settings.

The book discusses AI literacy, strengths and weaknesses of using ChatGPT in curriculum design, redesigning assessment for the AI era, developing institutional AI policies, and the technical foundations of generative AI. It also includes examples, case scenarios, frameworks, and prompt-engineering guidance, with a strong emphasis on higher education. The text notes that many examples and cases are drawn from post-secondary contexts, though some ideas may be adapted to other educational levels.

Its main conclusion is that GenAI should be integrated thoughtfully as a human partner rather than as a replacement for educators. The authors argue for AI literacy, ethical and policy guidance, authentic assessment redesign, and a learner-centric approach that prioritizes feedback, integrity, and responsible use of AI in education.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a book chapter/preface-style descriptive and conceptual treatment of generative AI in higher education, not an empirical study. It contains no direct evaluation, comparison, or outcome measurement relevant to the retrieved topic.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effect is reported and no student achievement outcomes are measured. The text is informative and policy-oriented rather than evidence of impact on learning.
